title: Cell Lysis Protocol Without Detergents
author: Queenie Chan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k79czr6

steps.title: Maintain cells on ice
steps.instruction: Keep fresh or previously frozen cells on ice; use 5 × 10⁷ cells per sample.

steps.title: Lyse cells with water‑TFE
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1:1 (v/v) mixture of water and trifluoroethanol (TFE) and add it to the cells in a fume hood, working quickly because TFE evaporates rapidly; TFE is stored in NCE 435 (flammable cabinet). The original protocol called for 2 min sonication at 20 % duty cycle, output control 3 using an ultrasonic probe, but this is not used here. While this step is being performed, turn on the heat block and set it to 95 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add mixture to cells in fume hood; work quickly.
Note original sonication parameters (2 min, 20 % duty, output 3) are omitted.
Turn on heat block and set to 95 °C.

steps.title: Add TCEP
steps.instruction: Add tris(2‑carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP) to reach a final concentration of 10 mM; TCEP is stored in NCE 436 (‑20 °C freezer door).

steps.title: Add 2‑CAA and heat
steps.instruction: Add 2‑chloroacetamide to reach a final concentration of 40 mM (stock located in NCE 438 on chemical shelves) and incubate the mixture at 95 °C for 10 minutes in a heat block.

substeps.instruction: Place tube in heat block at 95 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Spin down debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at top speed on a benchtop centrifuge for 10 minutes; carefully collect and keep the supernatant.

steps.title: Add LysC digestion
steps.instruction: Add LysC protease at 1 µg per 50 µg of protein and incubate for 2 hours (02:00:00) in an incubator (temperature not specified).

steps.title: Add trypsin digestion
steps.instruction: Add trypsin at 1 µg per 50 µg of protein and incubate overnight (minimum 16 hours, 16:00:00) in an incubator (temperature not specified).

steps.title: Measure protein concentration
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration using Coomassie reagent, aliquot the desired amount for downstream work, and avoid freezing any unused protein because it may precipitate upon thawing.
